messages.text:
Agenda for 10 today at the office:
• May column: two river claims in the running, we'll pick one
• Summer: any weeks you'll be away?
• Fall features: early thoughts welcome, rough is fine
see you at 10. nothing booked for summer yet - probably a long weekend up the shore in July. will bring a fall idea or two.
From this morning's edit meeting: May's column will be one of the two river claims. I'll post the pick here once I see which one is still spreading. Copy is due the 20th either way.
works - I'll open a file on both so I'm not starting cold.
May pick: the "Mississippi is America's dirtiest river" graphic is making the rounds again, and a city council candidate shared it this week. Want it for the column? Copy to me by the 20th.
yes, I'll take it - reads like a toxic-release ranking with the context sanded off. will trace where it started before I call anyone.
Perfect. Rating is your call, as always.
traced it - a 2014 advocacy ranking built on EPA's Toxics Release Inventory, sorted by total pounds discharged under permit. biggest river, most outfalls, top of the list.
So it's ranking size more than dirt. Leaning Misleading?

misleading. pounds discharged isn't concentration - the state's own assessments have the metro reach meeting most standards most of the time. the real trouble is sediment and nutrients. that's the story under the meme.
"The Buckthorn Line" is accepted. No more edits from me, so go ahead and invoice the fee.
thanks - invoiced this morning. INV-2026-030, $3,200.00, sent to AP.
Copy desk is asking for the May column Wednesday instead of Friday. They want to clear the decks before Memorial Day weekend. Doable?
doable - draft's mostly there, just waiting on one EPA table. you'll have it wed.
it's in the CMS - rated misleading, sources listed at the bottom. sending you a short note by email too.
Got it. Reading tonight, notes tomorrow.
Notes on the May column are in your email. Two small ones, both up top.
both done - group's named in the second graf now, waterway count right after. revised copy is in the CMS.

Morning. Agenda for 10:
• May column: copy desk was glad to get it early
• June column: leaning toward the viral ice-out thread, but open to others
• Art: Lena wants a map or chart with every column this summer, so bring ideas
see you at 10. bringing two backups in case ice-out doesn't pan out. maps i can do most months - charts only when the numbers earn one.
Thanks for coming in today. I'll post the ice-out claim in #factcheck once I've rechecked the share count on the original thread.
good. I'll pull the DNR's ice-out tables this week either way.
For the ice-out column: is the DNR data free to use, or do we need to license it?
free - the DNR posts ice-out dates lake by lake as public data. I'll cite the page and the date I pulled it.
Your June pick: 'Ice-out came a month early on every Minnesota lake.' The April thread it came from is past 9K shares. Can you get me a draft by Wed the 17th?
will do - by the 17th. 'every' is doing a lot of work in that sentence. the DNR keeps ice-out dates and medians for hundreds of lakes, so this one's checkable.
early read: metro lakes went out roughly two to three weeks ahead of their medians. up north, plenty were within a few days of normal. a month early holds for a handful of lakes, not every lake.
Partly true, then? Or does 'every' tip it into Misleading?
partly true. the warm spring was real and so were the early dates - it's 'every' and 'a month' that don't hold. I'll spell out which kinds of lakes came close.

Weekend reading: the Metro Lakes Watershed District put out its 2025 water-quality report on Thursday. The release says four lakes are over the state chloride standard. Is there a fall feature in it for you? No rush - Monday's fine.

could be. I already asked their press office for the site-level data - it goes through a request form, about 10 business days. also, Table 3 is a scanned image, so the numbers can't be copied out of it.
Trend, or one bad year?

not solid yet. The v2 errata on p. 3 change which sites are over 230 mg/L. I still have to go through the Oct 8 v2 against the June v1 line by line. Until that's done, the site claims stay as the tracker has them: C02 and C04 both show Verified.
:+1: Fine for Fri. With the re-rank and the v2 check added, does Nov 20 still hold for filing?
it holds. I'll file the morning of Nov 20. Top 5 to you fri, and the v1-v2 notes land in the tracker as I go.
hiya! for the ice-out column - do you have any shots of lake ice breaking up? 📸 if not, ok if i pull one from the DNR archive?
nothing usable from me this spring. DNR archive is fine - credit Minnesota DNR by name in the caption, not 'file photo.'
got it - Minnesota DNR by name. map's going with one dot per lake, and the lake table is final. updated mock goes in the art folder by tomorrow ✨
draft is up - partly true, with ice-out dates against the medians broken out by region.
Just read it. The regional breakdown is what makes it work. Running it as is.

sat in on SEJ's records-request webinar at noon. emailed you the three points that matter for the column, Hana. short version - when a viral claim cites an agency, ask for the data file behind it, not the press release.
Good notes - thanks. I replied to your fee question by email.

For everyone: Owen adapted SEJ's sample records-request letter for the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act. It's in the freelancer folder now, credited to SEJ. Start from it for any column that needs agency data.

Morning, Owen. Agenda for 10 at the office:
• July fact-check column
• Fall features - bring the road-salt idea
• Summer schedules
see you at 10. heads-up - I'm offline fri through sun, camping up the shore. back on email and slack monday.
Thanks for coming in this morning. I'll post July's claim in #factcheck early next week, so nothing from me before Monday. Enjoy the North Shore.
thanks. back at the desk monday - I'll grab the claim once it's up.
July's claim if you want it: "Minnesota has lost half its wetlands since 2000." A few conservation groups we like have been sharing it, so expect some heat if it doesn't hold up. Due Wed, July 22.
on it. hunch is someone grafted the historic loss figure onto a recent date. starting with the DNR's wetland status and trends reports.

hunch holds. paid $19.90 for a month of newspapers.com - the "half" figure has been in print since the 1980s, and it's the loss since settlement, mostly to farm drainage. DNR status and trends data since 2006 show net change of a fraction of a percent per three-year cycle. false as written.
That'll sting for the groups sharing it. Can you lead with the real loss so it doesn't read like we're saying wetlands are fine?
yes - that was the plan. the real number is bad enough on its own. the column is about the date, not the damage.
Two hed options for the wetlands column are at the top of the draft doc. Can you pick one by end of day?
the second. the first puts "half" in the hed - anyone who stops reading there walks away with the claim we're rating false.
filed. rated false, with the historic loss up top as you asked. sources are in the email I just sent.
Got it, thanks. I'll read it first thing tomorrow.
Morning. Read the wetlands column - it holds up. One small add, details in your email: a sentence near the end on what the state still loses every year to drainage and development.
added a graf near the end - net flat isn't the same as nothing happening. updated draft is in the CMS.

Morning, Owen. Agenda for 10:
• August column - probably a heat claim
• fall features lineup
• art for the August column
see you at 10 - I'll bring a couple of heat claims to compare.
From this morning's edit meeting: August is a heat claim. I'll post the pick here next week. Copy due Wed the 19th. Lena, plan on a map with this one.
ooh, a map ✨ holding a half page for it. send the data whenever the claim's set 🗺️
will do - as soon as the claim's picked.
Here's the August pick, from a heat-wave explainer that's been all over my feed this week: "Downtown nights are 15°F hotter than the suburbs." Feels half right. Copy by the 19th still work?
half right is my guess too. the heat island is real - the question is 15 compared to what, and on which nights. the 19th is fine.
hiya! heat map mock for the august column is in the layout folder ✨ can you check the legend before it goes to Hana? and is "downtown core" ok as the map label?

looked at it. the legend steps are uneven - 4 degrees, then 6, then 4 - and that makes it read hotter than the data. even them out, please. and just "downtown" on the label. the sensor sites don't line up with any official core boundary.

thanks ✨ steps are even now, whole degrees all the way up, and the label just says "downtown." also switched the map to show difference from the airport station, with both summer averages spelled out in the legend. new mock goes to Hana monday.

the university's sensor network has downtown running 13 to 15 degrees warmer than farm fields on the hottest, calmest nights. a typical summer night is more like 5 to 7 - and less than that against the inner-ring suburbs.
So 15 is the worst night against open country, not a typical night against the suburbs. Partly true works for me.
column's in - partly true. I kept the worst-night number in because those are the nights that put people in the hospital.
Good call keeping that. Copy desk has it Friday.

Morning, Owen. Agenda for 10:
• September column: which claim we take on
• Fall features: one slot still open, filing in November
• 2027 planning: first pass, nothing final yet
see you at 10. might have something for that november slot - i'll bring it.

Good meeting. Send me the road-salt idea in writing when it's ready. A few paragraphs is plenty. I'll hold the November slot through mid-September. September's claim goes up in #factcheck after Labor Day.
on the salt idea - you'll have a pitch next week. want to read the district's june report properly first.
pitch is in your inbox - winter road salt and the metro lakes, the one I floated at the last edit meeting. no rush.
Read the salt pitch - I'm in. I still have to clear the fee upstairs, so the assignment letter may take a week or two.
great, thanks - I'll pull the district's older water-quality reports in the meantime.
September candidate: "Superior is warming faster than any lake on Earth." It's on a brewery's coasters now, which is how you know it's everywhere. I'd need it by Wed the 23rd.
ha. sure - there's real research under this one, so my guess is it lands at needs context, not false. starting with the papers. the 23rd works.

early read: it traces to a 2007 paper finding Superior's summer surface water was warming faster than the air over the region. global surveys since then put Superior among the fast warmers - not alone at the top. and summer surface water isn't the whole lake.
Needs context it is. Let's leave the brewery out, though. They didn't start it, they just printed it.
agreed - the coasters are just how it got to your desk. the column's about the claim, not who repeats it.

Salt in the Lakes is official. Owen, the assignment letter went to your email this morning: about 3,000 words on winter road-salt use and what it's doing to metro lakes, due Fri Nov 20. Lena has art and layout. Let's keep reporting, edits and art for it in this channel.
yay, official! ✨ i've penciled in a chart sidebar and field photos so far. should i plan on district maps too? 📸

maps, yes - the district's 2025 water-quality report has a sampling-site map, and it's public. charts I'd rather build from numbers I've checked. field photos would come out of a weekend sampling day, probably in October. I'll flag things here as they come in.

interview request is out to Dr. Elise Marchand at the Lake Superior Freshwater Institute in Duluth, who studies chloride in Superior tributaries. asked for a background call in the next week or so, then a longer in-person interview in early November.
Good get if Marchand says yes. Send me a travel estimate before you book anything.
claims tracker is up in Airtable - Salt in the Lakes base, with tables for claims, sources and sites. Hana, the invite's in your email. Lena, I'll pull numbers from it for the art once they're solid.
Got the Airtable invite and I'm in. Having claims and sources split out like that is exactly what I need for the fact-check file.
good. the claims table is rough for now - I'll tidy it as the reporting comes in.
September's filed - rated needs context, with what each study actually measured spelled out in plain terms.
Thanks, Owen. Into the copy queue it goes.

Dr. Elise Marchand at the Lake Superior Freshwater Institute agreed to talk. Background call is Wed Sep 30 at 2, and she's fine with me recording it. She's open early November for a longer sit-down in Duluth. Hana - once we pin a date I'll price the trip and send you the numbers before I book anything.
salt advance landed this morning - $2,250, the first half. thanks for getting it signed off so fast.
Good - glad it landed before the weekend. If anything on the remittance looks off, tell me and I'll take it up with accounting.

hiya! production schedule for the salt package ✨
• Wed Oct 28: rough layout pdf to Hana and Owen
• Fri Nov 13: art list and photo selects
• Fri Nov 20: copy in
• Mon Nov 30: first pages out for the fact read
• Thu Dec 3: final proofs
• Tue Dec 8: off to the printer
also, the 2027 production calendar is live: <https://staff.northcurrentmag.com/production/2027|2027 production calendar>
two qs for Owen: does Nov 13 work for art? and is it still just the chart sidebar, or chart plus a site map?

nov 13 works. still the chart sidebar - built straight from the district's own tables, no eyeballing. and yes to a small site map. most readers couldn't point to these lakes. the district publishes one, i'll send it over.
Thanks, Lena - the schedule works for me. We'll walk through the 2027 calendar at the edit meeting next Tue (Oct 6, 10 a.m.). Owen, look over the fact-check deadlines in it before then.
yay 🎉 owen, for the map: quarter page or half? and lakes labeled by name or by the district's site codes?
quarter page is plenty. lake names on the map, site codes in a small key.
perfect, quarter page with a key ✨ pinning the schedule to the channel now
Lena, the 2027 calendar has the February issue closing Mon Jan 4 - our first day back from the holiday break. Can we push it to the end of that week?
ooh good catch! checking with the printer today, will have it updated before tues ✨

good background call with marchand this afternoon. groundwater came up a lot, and it changes how i'll frame part of the piece. she'll sit for a longer interview in duluth, probably the first week of november.
Great. Will she be on the record in Duluth?
yes - on the record and fine with being recorded. she'll speak to the chloride science and her own tributary work, not to the district's program.
hiya! still on for 11? ✨ i'll have the salt spread grid up on the big screen. can you bring whatever the district has published - report tables, any charts, and the site map if it's handy?
still on. i'll bring the district's 2025 report so we can go through the tables together - haven't pulled the site map file yet.
update: February close is now Fri Jan 8 - printer's fine with it 🎉 same link as before
thanks - jan 8 gives the february fact-check a real week after the holidays.
thanks for coming in!! ✨ i'm roughing out the chart sidebar and the quarter-page map this week. can you send me the district's site map once you track it down? 🗺️

dr. marchand penciled me in for thu nov 5 at 9:30 - in person, at the lake superior freshwater institute in duluth. plan is to fly up wed nov 4 and come home fri nov 6. hana, i'll have travel numbers for tuesday's edit meeting.
Works for me. Bring the lab quotes too and we'll go through Duluth and the split samples together on Tuesday.

both labs are lined up for the oct 10 split samples. riverside analytical (coon rapids) quoted $384.00 for the four; northstar environmental (bloomington) is $65 a sample, so $260.00 - $644 all in. picking up kits next week, dropping samples mon oct 12. both go on my visa and i'll bill north current after.

Morning! Here's what I have for 10:
• Salt in the Lakes check-in
• Duluth and lab expenses
• our 2027 features budget (still a draft)
• November fact-check topic
• winter and spring: what you can take on
see you at 10. bringing both lab quotes and a rough duluth number - airfare plus two hotel nights.

Recap from this morning's edit meeting, mostly for Lena:
• Salt in the Lakes is still due Fri Nov 20
• Your dates hold: rough layout Oct 28, art selects Nov 13
• Owen's Duluth trip (Nov 4-6) for the Marchand interview is approved
noted ✨ rough layout the 28th, selects the 13th, both on my calendar. holding room in the spread for a chart sidebar 📊
Still no claim for the November column. If you see one making the rounds, drop the link here.

station map for the salt spread - the district's public one: <https://www.metrolakeswd.org/monitoring/stations|MLWD monitoring stations>. lake names on the map, site codes in the key, like we talked about.
perfect, thank you!! ✨ i'll rough in the map this week and share a first pass here 📐

both labs' bottle kits are in hand - riverside's came yesterday, northstar's this morning. sampling sat at four district sites, from shore and pier only. district says grab samples don't need a permit. splits go to both labs mon morning.

heads-up - the district posted a revised 2025 water-quality report this afternoon, errata page and all. haven't gone through it line by line yet. media call fri 10-11 on the revision and the 2027 draft budget. i'll be on it.
Owen - the district posted its revised 2025 water-quality report today. Does it change any of the numbers we're already using in the tracker?
don't know yet. i've got both versions saved but haven't been through the revision line by line. the side-by-side is on my list for next week.

just off the district media call. the 2027 draft budget has a bigger chloride line, and they've put a per-lake figure on monitoring - $7,400 a lake. Luis is sending the draft budget and the smart-salting summary later today.
Good. Is that budget public yet, or still a draft?

still a draft. Luis already sent it - the two tables i need are on scanned pages, 9 and 14. i've asked him two things: what each table covers, and whether the $7,400 includes equipment. numbers go in the tracker this afternoon.

heard back from Luis on both. the p. 14 table is 2021-25 chloride spending; the proposed 2027 line is on p. 9. the $7,400 per lake is contract-lab fees only - no equipment. page refs are in the tracker. the budget stays a draft until the board adopts it in November, so it's "proposed" in copy.
Great - that's exactly the paper trail I want in the fact-check file.

split samples from saturday's four sites (COR-1, PEN-OUT, ODG-IN, SUM-1) went in at both labs this morning - Riverside in Coon Rapids, Northstar in Bloomington. results due next week. drop-off details are in your email.
October claim: "Monarchs crashed 90% this year." It's making the rounds, and the comments are full of "didn't see a single one in my yard." Can you file it by the 20th?
yes - the 20th works. my hunch is the 90 is the long-term decline at the winter colonies in Mexico, not a one-year drop. and an empty yard isn't a count.
Hey Owen - I left three questions for you in the tracker's Claims table: two on the budget claims, one on the snowmelt numbers. Nothing urgent.
thanks for the comments - answered the p. 14 one in the tracker. the other two need more digging, so I'll come back to those.
hiya! roughing out the monarch column page. ok to run the USFWS tagging photo with a credit line? 📸 and which way is the badge leaning - "misleading" or "needs context"?
re the monarch page - the USFWS photo is fine with a credit line. badge should be "needs context." "misleading" would claim more than the column does. hana has the final say once she's edited it.
Checking in on the monarch column - Lena needs final copy by Tue the 20th to get it into layout. Still on track?
still on track - draft to you fri, so you'll have monday for edits before lena's tuesday deadline.

lena - hana flagged a good one in the tracker. the district's storm-sewer station at the odegaard north inlet hit 1,020 mg/L in march 2025, during snowmelt - more than three times any lake mean in the report. worth a small chart next to the sidebar? I can send the table.
ooh yes ✨ a little spike chart would sit nicely under the sidebar. just that inlet or a few stations? and same colors as the sidebar?

just that one. the district only added inlet and outlet stations last year, so the report has a single winter of data - caption should say so. sidebar colors are fine, but give it its own axis starting at zero; on a shared scale the inlet would flatten the lakes. table coming once the monarch draft goes to hana fri.

confirmed. the 90% is roughly the long-term drop in forest area the colonies occupy in Mexico, measured from the mid-1990s peak. this winter's count doesn't exist yet - it comes out early next year. so "this year" is the misleading part.
Misleading, then. Lena wants to try a small chart of the winter counts alongside it.

duluth's booked - fly up wed nov 4, home fri nov 6. marchand is thu at 9:30. flight $289.40 + lakewalk inn $371.88 for the two nights = $661.28, under the $800 cap. both are on my visa; receipts go in with the invoice.
fyi for the schedule - i'm in duluth wed nov 4 through fri nov 6 for the marchand interview. flight and hotel are booked. lena, the art list still comes to you by fri nov 13.
noted ✨ nov 13 stays circled for the art list. safe travels up north next month 📸

Possible November pick: a Facebook chart going around since last night says "Chloride in our lakes has DOUBLED since 2020" and credits the district's 2025 report. Shares are climbing fast. DMing you too. Should we reach out to whoever posted it?

Have you seen this chart? "Chloride in our lakes has DOUBLED since 2020." It's been picking up shares since last night, and the footer says "Data: MLWD 2025 report." Could it be our November fact-check? And do we want to reach out to whoever made it?

saw it this morning. the jump looks too big to me, but i haven't checked it against the report yet.
i'd keep it out of the column - it cites the district's 2025 report, the same source the feature runs on, so it belongs in the feature.
and hold off on contacting the poster. i know her through salt watch and would rather talk to her myself once i've been through the numbers.
Makes sense, it goes in the feature. I'll find another item for November. The poster is yours to handle.
thanks. logging it in the claims table as unverified so nobody cites it by accident.
answered in DM - this one cites the same district report the salt feature runs on, so it goes in the feature, not the column. and let's leave the poster alone for now. i'll handle that part.
Agreed, feature not column, so no column art for this one. We still need a November claim. Drop candidates here.
hana - claims in the tracker are ranked for the salt-use draft. worth a look before i start the outline, if you have time.
Thanks. I'll go through them this weekend and flag anything that needs a second source.
riverside's results on the oct. 10 samples came in this morning - WO-26-10418. northstar's are due later this week, so i'm keeping both out of the tracker until theirs are in.
monarchs are in the CMS, rated misleading. the winter-count series for Lena's chart is in the source list - hectares by season. y-axis starts at zero, please.
Thanks - I'll read it this morning and pass the series to Lena.
fyi - strib has a salt-dome story up this morning: metro cities stocking up before winter, prices creeping up. it's supply and city budgets - nothing on the lakes or chloride. no overlap with ours.
Thanks for reading it. Sounds like we still have the lakes to ourselves.

northstar's report (NS-4471) came in this morning, so both labs are back. both are in the tracker, with each lab's method noted on its source entry. the numbers don't match - northstar runs higher at all four sites. going through both method sheets before i decide which one we cite.
lab fees for salt: riverside $384.00, northstar $260.00. $644.00 for the pair, under the $700 cap. both went on my visa - they'll be on the expense invoice.
Looking ahead to spring: would you take on a Lake Pepin sediment series? Three or four parts, running February through May.
No rush on an answer. I'm roughing out the 2027 features list and wanted to offer it to you before I ask anyone else.
duluth interview is set - dr. marchand, thu nov 5, 9:30 to 11:30, room 214 at the lake superior freshwater institute. flying up wed the 4th, back fri the 6th.

Recapping this morning for the channel: new angle is cleanup cost for the watershed districts, with salt use as context. Owen, can you re-rank the tracker against that and send me your top 5 claims by Friday?
two layout q's: does the chart sidebar survive the new angle? and should i hold space for a cost graphic? ✨
Sidebar stays - the viral chart is still the hook. Yes to a cost graphic, once Owen's top claims are set.
on it - re-ranking the claims in the tracker for the cleanup-cost angle. top 5 to you by fri.
Thanks. End of day Friday works.

One more thing for the salt fact-check file before your draft comes in. For the field tech who sampled with you on Oct 10, I need:
• name
• affiliation (employer or agency)
Can you put both here in writing so they're on record? Neither will run in the piece.
It's the same standard we used on the monarch column this month: anyone who handled samples or data gets a name and affiliation in the file. The file stays internal.
rough layout pdf for salt is up in the layout folder ✨ chart sidebar, site map and the cost graphic are still gray boxes. notes whenever you've had a look?

Can we do the salt edit meeting the week of Nov 9? In person at the office, about 90 minutes. With the move to the cleanup-cost angle, I'd like to walk through the structure together. What days and times work for you?
Mon through Thu is best for me. Mornings, or any time after 2.
hiya! for the viral chart sidebar, could you grab the original fb post? name, avatar and share count - it reads way more real than the chart on its own ✨
also - any field pics from sampling day with people in them? 📸
even just hands holding a sample bottle or someone at the waterline would make the opener feel real. and what credit line do you want on the field shots?
no rush - the sidebar's still a gray box in the rough layout. it's two columns wide, so a straight screenshot of the post would drop right in
